decision: measured both database entry paths instead of trusting the README
why: the README says the world seeds itself with 26 organisations, but that is only the Reset path; wanted to know what a fresh deploy actually gets
evidence: db/fixtures.sql vs db/seed.sql, counted in psql
result: bootstrap gives 0 suppliers, 0 lenders, 0 ERP invoices, 0 payables

decision: ran the whole suite before changing anything
why: needed a known-good line to measure against, not a guess about what was already broken
result: both exit 0, all green

decision: enriched db/fixtures.sql rather than pointing bootstrap at db/seed.sql
why: user picked a minimal starter over the full catalogue; seed.sql also walks 200 days of history and is not safe to replay on a cold start
result: 2 suppliers, 2 lenders, 24 ERP invoices, 0 payables

decision: wrote the fresh-world test before writing the world
why: an empty ERP register and an empty supplier dropdown compile and render fine, so only something that counts them catches it
result: red: expected 2 suppliers, found 0

decision: built the starter world on natural-predicate guards and md5 idempotency keys
why: ensure.ts races across serverless cold starts, so a second pass has to converge instead of paying the lenders twice
result: green: 13 assertions including the double-load replay

decision: derived the awaited actor from the existing transition table instead of branching per status in the page
why: the screen disables its buttons from that same table, so one source means the sentence and the controls cannot disagree
result: 6 new unit tests; mutation check confirmed 3 fail on broken code

decision: moved reference generation into one core module rather than adding a third copy of the padding
why: TP-2026-nnnn was already formatted in two components and regexed in a third file; the invoice suggestion would have been a fourth
result: 11 unit tests green, typecheck clean

decision: assertions were failing against a screen that plainly said the right thing
why: innerText returns rendered text and the headings are CSS-uppercased; suspected the check before the code and looked at the real page
result: 4 of 5 failures were the observation method, not the feature

decision: waited on the queue moving instead of on the button's success notice
why: a write revalidates the layout and unmounts the control that fired it, so its notice is not a thing to hold an assertion against
result: 10 of 10 steps green on the seeded world, exit 0

decision: built scripts/fresh.sh so the bootstrap world gets driven in a browser too
why: the seeded world is what every existing driver runs against, so without this the path a new deployment takes is only ever exercised in production, by the audience
result: fresh world exit 0: 24 invoices, 2 suppliers, TP-2026-0001 created and handed through the queue

decision: ran every suite against both worlds
why: the change touches the file that runs on every cold start, so a green unit suite alone would not have told me the app opens
evidence: npm test, verify:screens, verify:runbook, verify:demo, scripts/fresh.sh
result: all exit 0; runbook 38 steps in 53s

decision: found two faults in my own diff before asking anyone else
why: holders could come back empty when the admin deactivates the only account holding a role, and the whose-move test was derived twice
result: consolidated to one derivation; unheld-role case now names the gap

decision: ran four cleanup agents over the diff and took most of what they found
why: self-review had already missed a false claim in my own comment, so a second pass was worth the tokens
evidence: reuse, simplification, efficiency and altitude agents on the full diff
result: 9 findings adopted, 6 skipped with reasons

decision: onboarded the counterparties through ledger.post instead of writing app tables directly
why: that intent already creates the organisation, wallet, first user and eligibility; the anchor rows above cannot use it, these can
result: 13 assertions still green

decision: the reference generator was reading a projection that hides series members
why: readPayables filters series_id IS NULL, so the twelve TP-2026-05xx refs were invisible to a generator claiming to continue the series
result: create page now reads two columns instead of the whole priced book

decision: fixed a comment that claimed a consolidation I had not done
why: ROLE_LABELS said three screens were spelling roles independently, and I had migrated one; the claim was false either way I went
result: comment now says what the map is; attempt() refusals use it too

decision: dropped the key= remount on manual entry for an override in state
why: the remount discarded the supplier, face and terms already typed whenever the suggestion moved
result: no remount; edited-or-not is a null check

decision: turned down the WITH ORDINALITY suggestion after testing it
why: VALUES does not take WITH ORDINALITY in Postgres, and row_number over VALUES has no guaranteed order, which the runbook invoice depends on
evidence: psql: syntax error at or near WITH
result: kept explicit doc numbers

decision: left the seed/fixtures split, the shared browser driver and the one-button rewrite alone
why: each rewrites working verified code well past what was asked; noted for the user instead
result: open

decision: supersedes the U2 row: db/fixtures.sql:113-312 no longer resolves
why: the onboard_entity rewrite cut the file to 253 lines, so that line range points at the wrong thing now
result: pointer corrected, the claim itself still holds

decision: checked each commit stands on its own, not just the final tree
why: a four-commit split a reviewer cannot bisect is decoration
result: all three typecheck and pass 148 unit tests alone

decision: confirmed fresh.sh no longer takes down the server on :3100
why: that was the reviewer's finding and the README tells the reader to have that server running
result: still serving

decision: ran every suite once more against the four committed commits
why: the tree had moved since the last full pass, so the earlier green did not describe what is being handed over
evidence: npm test, verify:screens, verify:runbook, verify:demo, verify:fresh at 8c0615e
result: all five exit 0

decision: the independent reviewer found fresh.sh was not testing what its commit message claimed
why: it loaded the fixtures with psql first, so ensureWorld saw a ready world and returned before taking the lock; the run proved the data and not the mechanism
result: dropped the psql load; the app's own first requests do the bootstrap now

decision: made the fresh run fire three concurrent first requests
why: the advisory lock exists because two serverless instances can meet on an empty database, and one request at a time never reaches it
evidence: scripts/fresh.sh, asserts one world row after
result: tests the race the commit was actually about

decision: added a usability assertion to the end of db/fixtures.sql
why: every insert is guarded on state it expects, and a guard matching nothing skips silently and still commits, which is the empty demo this whole change exists to stop
evidence: db/fixtures.sql, proved it raises on a world with no counterparties
result: fails the first request loudly instead

decision: logging a pivot that was only in prose: declined moving reference allocation into post.sql
why: it would close a two-tabs-both-get-0154 race; I checked and the unique index already refuses the second with ADA26, so the stakes are low
evidence: db/schema.sql payable ref UNIQUE, db/post.sql ADA26
result: declined, disclosed

decision: the corrected fresh run failed first time, and the failure was mine
why: an orphaned next-server from an earlier run still held :3101, so the requests reached a stale server pointing at a database I had just recreated
result: fresh.sh now frees its own port; npx runs the server as a grandchild so killing $! left it alive

decision: second failure was a bare wait in my own script
why: wait with no arguments waits for every background job, and the server is one of them, so the script hung instead of proceeding to the driver
evidence: scripts/fresh.sh, wait now names the three request pids
result: run completes

decision: the application now bootstraps an empty database for real, under three concurrent first requests
why: this is the path a cold serverless instance takes and nothing was exercising it before
evidence: scripts/fresh.sh: 3 requests ok, one world row, then 10 driver steps
result: exit 0

decision: asked before cutting, because under 30 entries collides with PRD 12
why: the series lot costs 24 entries and needs 12 account-less suppliers, so the entry budget and the no-login-supplier ask were the same lever
evidence: AskUserQuestion, answer: shrink the series to 5
result: 5 members, one per interactive supplier

decision: rewrote db/seed.sql around the six payables PRD 12 actually names
why: the old seed added depth the PRD never asked for, and every extra row is one a presenter scrolls past on the explorer
result: all 17 seed assertions pass, PRD yields still reproduce exactly

decision: put an entry budget in the test rather than trusting the file to stay small
why: a seed grows one convenient row at a time, and nothing was measuring it
result: fails if it creeps back up

decision: the accounts test was finding its fixture in the seed instead of building one
why: it picked an account-less supplier to prove ADA31, and silently broke when the seed stopped having any
result: builds and removes its own now

decision: ran every suite against the slimmed seed
why: the runbook drives the seeded world hardest, so it was the real gate rather than the SQL tests
evidence: npm test, verify:screens, verify:runbook, verify:demo, verify:fresh
result: all exit 0; runbook 38 steps in 51s

decision: the runbook's new payable came out as TP-2026-0506, past the series members
why: the reference generator reads the whole payable table now, so it stepped over 0501-0505 instead of colliding
result: the earlier readReferencesInUse fix paying off

decision: revised PRD section 12 to five originators rather than leaving it contradicting the build
why: a specification the code knowingly ignores stops being worth reading; the assumptions entry becomes the record of why it moved
evidence: tokenised-payable-prd.md:293,299 plus a dated revision note
result: PRD and build now agree

decision: found docs/RUNBOOK.md still telling the presenter the lot holds twelve 15,000 tickets
why: I changed the seed last round and did not sweep the prose; a presenter would have read that aloud against a screen showing five
result: corrected to five 36,000 tickets

decision: swept every other reference to the twelve rather than just the two the user named
why: three code comments and an assumptions entry were also stale, and one of them claimed the seed still had twelve account-less suppliers
result: only historical quotations mention twelve now
